[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#normative-language-convention]

### Normative Language Convention

This document and all Component ABBs in this hierarchy use normative language per [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119):

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SHALL** | Mandatory — absolute obligation |
| **SHALL NOT** | Mandatory prohibition |
| **SHOULD** | Strongly recommended — deviation requires documented justification |
| **SHOULD NOT** | Strongly discouraged — deviation requires documented justification |
| **MAY** | Optional — permitted but not required |

> **Exception and Waiver Process**: Teams that cannot meet a SHALL requirement must submit a risk acceptance or waiver request through the established enterprise governance process. Waivers require documented risk justification and approval from appropriate security leadership or designated delegate. Temporary waivers must include a remediation timeline.

### ABB Context

- **This document**: Composite ABB — defines the full Endpoint Security architectural hierarchy and its Component ABBs
- **Domain**: Endpoint Security — Security Domain
- **Capability Statement**: Establishes the architectural framework for governing the security posture of all managed endpoint devices through asset inventory, configuration governance, protection, detection, mobile management, vulnerability management, device trust, privilege management, data protection, and telemetry capabilities, in alignment with Zero Trust device posture principles

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- All managed endpoint device populations: workstations, laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops, servers
- Endpoint asset lifecycle: discovery, inventory, classification, and decommissioning
- Configuration hardening baselines, compliance monitoring, and drift detection
- Endpoint protection and prevention architecture
- Endpoint behavioral detection, investigation, and response architecture
- Mobile and remote device policy enforcement and posture management
- Endpoint vulnerability discovery, prioritization, and remediation tracking
- Device trust signals and posture assessment for Zero Trust access decision infrastructure
- Endpoint privilege governance and just-enough-access architecture
- Endpoint data encryption and data loss prevention architecture
- Endpoint telemetry collection, normalization, and security operations integration

**Out of Scope**:
- Vendor product selection and implementation-specific configuration (Phase E–F)
- Physical access control and device hardware supply chain
- Identity lifecycle management, user authentication, and authorization (see [GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01](../Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md))
- Network segmentation and network-layer access controls (see Network Security domain)
- Data classification and data governance at the platform layer (see Information Security domain)
- Security controls, configuration mandates, and audit requirements (belong in `standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-1-universal-endpoint-asset-registration]

### CR-1: Universal Endpoint Asset Registration

All managed endpoint devices SHALL be registered in the enterprise endpoint asset inventory before being permitted access to enterprise resources. The registration record SHALL include at minimum: device identity (hardware identifier or managed certificate), device type and operating system, assigned owner or responsible team, current managed status, and last-known compliance state. Devices that cannot be registered due to architectural constraints (legacy hardware, OT devices) SHALL be documented as exceptions with a defined risk mitigation plan.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-2-configuration-baseline-enforcement]

### CR-2: Configuration Baseline Enforcement

Every managed device population SHALL have an applicable, version-controlled configuration hardening baseline. The baseline SHALL be enforced through automated policy deployment mechanisms rather than manual configuration. Configuration compliance state SHALL be continuously monitored, and devices with material configuration drift SHALL be flagged for remediation within the defined operational SLA or have their access tier reduced by the Zero Trust Policy Decision Point.
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-3-endpoint-detection-coverage]

### CR-3: Endpoint Detection Coverage

Endpoint detection and response capability SHALL be deployed to all managed workstations, laptops, and servers. Mobile devices SHALL have equivalent behavioral monitoring coverage through the MDM/UEM platform. Endpoints without active, healthy EDR or equivalent detection coverage SHALL be treated as posture-degraded for access decision purposes.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-4-device-posture-integration-with-zero-trust]

### CR-4: Device Posture Integration with Zero Trust

Endpoint security posture signals — including configuration compliance, EPP/EDR agent health, patch state, and management enrollment status — SHALL be integrated with the enterprise Zero Trust Policy Decision Point. Access to resources classified as sensitive SHALL require a current, passing device posture assessment. Posture evaluation SHALL be continuous and not limited to authentication time.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-5-least-privilege-on-endpoints]

### CR-5: Least Privilege on Endpoints

Standard user endpoints SHALL NOT have standing local administrative access. Administrative access to endpoint operating systems and management functions SHALL be provided through time-bounded, approval-gated privilege elevation mechanisms. All privilege elevation events SHALL be logged and forwarded to the endpoint telemetry pipeline.
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-6-endpoint-data-encryption]

### CR-6: Endpoint Data Encryption

All managed workstations and laptops SHALL have full-disk encryption enabled and verified as active. Mobile devices with access to enterprise data SHALL have device encryption enabled and enforced through MDM policy. Removable media used for enterprise data SHALL be encrypted through an enterprise-managed mechanism.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#cr-7-telemetry-forwarding-to-security-operations]

### CR-7: Telemetry Forwarding to Security Operations

Endpoint security events from all managed devices SHALL be collected and forwarded to the enterprise security information and event platform. The telemetry schema SHALL be documented and version-controlled. Telemetry collection SHALL be continuously monitored for pipeline health, and gaps in coverage SHALL be treated as operational incidents.

## Adjacent Domain Interfaces

| Adjacent Domain | Interface | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [Identity Security — GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01](../Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md) | Device posture signals → Zero Trust PDP; device certificates issued by endpoint management consumed by identity infrastructure | Endpoint provides device trust; Identity provides user trust; access decisions combine both |

| Network Security | Device managed-status and posture compliance → Network Access Control | Endpoint provides health signal; Network enforces access or quarantine |
| Information Security | Data classification policies → Endpoint DLP enforcement | Information Security defines classification; Endpoint enforces at device layer |

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md#zero-trust-architecture-alignment]

## Zero Trust Architecture Alignment

This Composite ABB realizes the **Devices** pillar of Zero Trust (NIST SP 800-207). The following table maps each Component ABB to its Zero Trust contribution:

| Component ABB | Zero Trust Role |
|---|---|
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-ASSET-2.4.01 | Device identity registry — prerequisite for any device trust evaluation |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CONFIG-2.4.02 | Configuration compliance signal for posture assessment |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EPP-2.4.03 | Protection agent health status as posture signal |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EDR-2.4.04 | Detection coverage and agent health as posture signal |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-MDM-2.4.05 | Mobile enrollment and policy compliance as device trust signal |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-VULN-2.4.06 | Vulnerability exposure as risk-adjusted posture signal |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-DEVICE-TRUST-2.4.07 | **Core Zero Trust integration layer** — aggregates all posture signals for PDP consumption |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EPM-2.4.08 | Privilege context contributes to behavioral anomaly detection |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EDP-2.4.09 | Data protection compliance as posture element |
| GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-TELEM-2.4.10 | Continuous behavioral signal stream for ongoing trust evaluation |
